A1.justification: Both PDFs provide readable text, equations, figures and tables for the same SmartEraser work. v3 retains v2's main paper and adds Appendices A–E. Citation renumbering and relocated references can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark results, component ablations, qualitative evaluations and a 30-participant user study in Section 4.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds quantitative ablations, qualitative comparisons and application and failure cases in its appendices.

M1.justification: The masked-region guidance, dataset construction, mask enhancement, visual guidance and training objective remain unchanged. Appendix B explicitly supplies implementation details of the existing MLP. The progressive-remasking example reuses the same eraser.

E1.justification: Training sources and the three named benchmarks are retained. Figures 12–13 add scene-text erasure and partial-object removal, while Figure 15 examines crowded masks and progressive removal. Occlusion was already illustrated in v2, so Figure 14 extends existing coverage.

E2.justification: Figure 10 newly evaluates Instruct-Pix2Pix and Inst-Inpaint, previously only cited or discussed. Figures 19–20 also include ZITS++, MAT, BLD, RePaint and SD-Inpaint in real-world-mask comparisons previously showing LaMa, CLIPAway and PowerPaint. These extensions are qualitative; quantitative benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Figure 10 adds a qualitative comparison using textual requests for instruction-based baselines and masks for SmartEraser. Figure 15 tests sequential user remasking. Existing benchmark splits, metrics, training budget and user-study procedures remain unchanged; newly disclosed implementation settings do not establish changed experiments.

E4.justification: v2 quantitatively ablates components only on RORD-Val. v3 extends these ablations to DEFACTO-Val and Syn4Removal-Val in Tables 6–7, adds qualitative ablations in Figure 11, and examines partial removal, occlusion and crowded-mask failure with progressive recovery. This substantially broadens evidence about component effectiveness and operating limits.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. The added ablation tables retain the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 are unchanged. Tables 6–7 add baseline and intermediate ablation results, including DEFACTO-Val FID values of 10.125, 7.142 and 4.701 for baseline, +RG and +ME; their full-model endpoints repeat existing results. Additional images report instruction-method comparisons, successful special-task removals, and incomplete crowded-mask removal followed by progressive recovery.

T1.justification: Appendix A adds the explicit mathematical definition thres_c = min(b, max(S_c) - d) for classwise CLIP filtering thresholds in Equation 10. This formalizes previously unspecified filtering details. Equations 1–9 remain unchanged, and no theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about masked-region guidance, Syn4Removal and superior removal quality and robustness. The supplementary evidence does not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix E newly explains that crowded masks can cause target objects to be mistaken for background, producing incomplete removal, and recommends progressive masking. Appendix D also explains how the existing IoU-based synthesis permits some occlusion. The main interpretations of component benefits remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices A–B materially expand implementation disclosure: CLIP threshold constants, minimum image dimensions, aspect-ratio and 85% instance-coverage filters, 512×512 processing, background-source counts, and the residual MLP's two linear layers, LayerNorm, GELU and 768-dimensional features. These fill substantial specification gaps without establishing changes to the underlying implementation.

R1.justification: v3 adds Hendrycks and Gimpel's GELU reference for the MLP description. Other cited works match after renumbering, and Section 2's research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The main prose and section sequence remain unchanged apart from citation numbering and the version stamp. v3 adds an organized supplement covering dataset details, framework details, samples, experiments and limitations, with references following it.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands the visual presentation with the MLP diagram, dataset-triplet montage, additional ablation tables, extensive comparison grids and special-case and failure illustrations in Figures 9–20 and Tables 6–7. Existing figures and tables retain their layouts.

improvement.justification: v2 leaves consequential filtering and MLP specifications unstated and quantitatively tests component contributions only on RORD-Val. Appendices A–B and Tables 6–7 substantially strengthen reproducibility and validation across the retained benchmarks, while Appendix E documents a concrete failure boundary and workaround. These address important documentation and evaluation gaps. The added special-task and instruction-method comparisons remain qualitative, limiting conclusions about their generality.
